content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"The sun principally symbolizes God’s radiant glory and, most characteristically, Jesus Christ as the Sun of Righteousness; it can also signify the glorified righteous and governing figures.","book_summary":"The sun identifies the Father as the original source of light, while the righteous shine derivatively like the sun in His kingdom.","consensus_core_identification":"God, especially Christ, as the source and manifestation of divine light, righteousness, and glory.","book_core_identification":"The Father specifically as the source of all lesser light, with the righteous reflecting that light.","core_relation":"BOOK_NARROWS","extension_relation":"BOOK_SUBSET","boundary_disagreement":"The book restricts the primary divine identification to the Father rather than retaining the consensus’s broader God/especially-Christ identification. This preserves the consensus’s general identification while changing its principal personal specification and excluding many other contextual senses.","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"Because the blind consensus repeatedly makes Christ—not merely God generically—the principal identification, one could view the book’s Father-specific identification as replacing the central referent and therefore as divergent.
